slo_title: Perform traversal and searching operations in singly linked lists.

mcq.q: When inserting a node at the beginning of a singly linked list, what must be done first

options.A: Make the new node point to the current head
options.B: Make the new node point to NULL

mcq.answer_text: Make the new node point to NULL

mcq.q: The system needs to search for a specific student’s attendance record. What will happen if the student is at the end of the list

options.A: The search will be completed in O(1) time
options.B: The system must traverse through the entire list in O(n) time
options.C: The system can access the record directly using an index
options.D: The search will always fail if the student is not in the first half of the list

mcq.answer_text: The system must traverse through the entire list in O(n) time

mcq.q: A user wants to add a new song to the end of the playlist. What will be the time complexity if the app does not store the tail pointer
A high-priority ticket needs to be processed before all other tickets. Where should it be inserted

options.A: At the beginning of the linked list
options.B: At the end of the linked list
options.C: In the middle of the linked list
options.D: The system cannot handle priority-based insertions

mcq.answer_text: At the beginning of the linked list

mcq.q: Which pointer needs to be updated when inserting at the beginning of a singly linked list

options.B: Next pointer of the new node

sq.q: Explain the algorithm to insert an element in an Linked List at the beginning. Write the steps clearly and provide a dry run with a sample input
answer: Overflow condition occurs when AVAIL = NULL or no free memory cell is present in the system. At this condition the program must give an appropriate message. There are 4 cases:
Case 1: The new node is inserted at the beginning.
Case 2: The new node is inserted at the end.
Case 3: The new node is inserted after a given node.
Case 4: The new node is inserted before a given node
ALGORITHM: The new node is inserted at the beginning of the node
